result.title: VANDAM: Viewing a nucleotide sequence with DNA molecular priors
result.summary: Contemporary Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs) rely on a DNA-as-a-string paradigm that employs masked token prediction objectives for pretraining. However, this abstraction does not explicitly model the biochemical, structural, and physical properties essential to biological function. Many molecular properties can be estimated from sequence using established biophysical models, so their utility lies not in providing an independent modality, but in introducing priors that training objectives can explicitly exploit. We introduce VANDAM, a framework that extends the training of GFMs with DNA molecular priors. In self-supervised training, VANDAM predicts regional molecular properties from pooled representations. When functional labels are available and can reward retaining molecular priors, local features are additionally injected at the input. VANDAM consistently improves downstream performance across four architecture families and nine held-out genomic tasks by complementing token-based objectives. Probing experiments further demonstrate that the use of molecular priors generalizes to other unseen molecular properties.

AI.brief_summary: VANDAM 在基因组基础模型的自监督训练中引入 DNA 分子先验：既让池化表示预测区域分子性质，又在有功能标签时把局部特征注入输入，从而补充掩码 token 目标。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作与视觉无关，但其「从池化表示预测区域属性、并在下游标签可奖励时注入局部特征」的监督设计，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及辅助监督如何影响状态内容提供可核查线索。
